newsitem.title: USA: Colorado awarded $10 mln for highway, bridge plans.
newsitem.headline: Colorado awarded $10 mln for highway, bridge plans.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena said on Thursday that the department allocated three Federal Highway Administration discretionary grants totaling $10 million to the state of Colorado for highway and bridge projects.

In addition, Pena announced the award of $1.5 million in Federal Transit Administration funds to the Denver Regional Transportation District to begin construction of the southwest extension of the Denver light rail system.

"President Clinton is committed to investing in transportation, which strengthens the economy and improves the quality of life," Pena said. "This funding will make transportation more efficient for residents of Colorado."

The $1.5 million grant to the Regional Transportation District represented the first installment of a $120 million full funding grant agreement to extend the Central Corridor light rail system by 8.7 miles. A full funding grant agreement is the federal government's commitment to support a transit project over the course of several fiscal years, contingent upon the availability of funds.
